name: PCI DSS v4.0: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard

controls.title: Network Security Controls - Restrict Inbound and Outbound Traffic
controls.description: Restrict inbound and outbound traffic to that which is necessary for the cardholder data environment, and specifically deny all other traffic.
controls.guidance: All firewall and router rule sets must implement a deny-all default stance. Rules permitting 'ip any any' or equivalent unrestricted traffic are strictly non-compliant. Each rule must be documented with a business justification.

controls.title: Restrict Inbound Traffic to CDE
controls.description: Restrict inbound traffic to system components in the cardholder data environment (CDE) to only that which is necessary.
controls.guidance: Ingress filtering on all perimeter devices must be configured so that only explicitly permitted services reach the CDE. Management plane access (SSH, HTTPS) must be restricted to dedicated administrative subnets.

controls.title: Configuration Standards - System Hardening
controls.description: Develop configuration standards for all system components. Assure that these standards address all known security vulnerabilities and are consistent with industry-accepted system hardening standards.
controls.guidance: Default credentials must be changed on all network devices. SNMP community strings 'public' and 'private' are prohibited. Unused services and ports must be disabled.

controls.title: Encrypt All Non-Console Administrative Access
controls.description: All non-console administrative access is encrypted using strong cryptography.
controls.guidance: Telnet, rlogin, rsh, and HTTP-based management must be disabled. Only SSH v2 and HTTPS with TLS 1.2+ are permitted for device management access.

controls.title: Security Patches and Updates
controls.description: All system components are protected from known vulnerabilities by installing applicable security patches/updates.
controls.guidance: Critical security patches must be applied within one month of release. Vendor-recommended firmware and software versions should be tracked for all network devices.

controls.title: Strong Authentication for Users and Administrators
controls.description: All user IDs and authentication credentials for non-consumer users are managed according to access control policy.
controls.guidance: Local user accounts with default passwords must be removed or disabled. Password complexity and minimum length requirements must be enforced on all network device user accounts.

controls.title: Audit Log Generation
controls.description: Audit logs capture all individual user access to cardholder data and all actions by any individual with root or administrative privileges.
controls.guidance: Logging must be enabled on all network devices. Syslog must be forwarded to a central log server. Login/logout events, configuration changes, and privilege escalation must all be captured.

controls.title: Retain Audit Logs for at Least 12 Months
controls.description: Retain audit log history for at least 12 months, with at least the most recent three months available for immediate analysis.
controls.guidance: Logging infrastructure must have sufficient capacity and retention policy configured. Logs must be stored on a separate, protected server with integrity controls.
